title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Provisions on the Supervision and Administration of Litigation Fees
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Provisions on the Supervision and Administration of Litigation Fee Collection

Fa Fa [2007] No. 30

To all local people's courts at various levels nationwide, all military courts, all railway transportation intermediate courts and basic courts, all maritime courts, and all courts at various levels in the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

To further strengthen and improve the supervision and administration of litigation fee collection by people's courts and ensure the correct implementation of the Measures on the Payment of Litigation Costs, the Supreme People's Court has formulated the Provisions on the Supervision and Administration of Litigation Fee Collection (hereinafter referred to as the "Provisions"). The Provisions are hereby issued to you for your earnest implementation in light of actual circumstances.

September 20, 2007

Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Supervision and Administration of Litigation Fee Collection

To further strengthen and improve the supervision and administration of litigation fee collection by people's courts, prevent and investigate illegal fee collection, and protect the lawful rights and interests of the parties, these Provisions are formulated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law, the Administrative Procedure Law, and the Measures on the Payment of Litigation Costs.

Article 1 The scope and standards of litigation fee collection shall strictly comply with the Measures on the Payment of Litigation Costs, and no increase in the fee collection standards shall be allowed.

Article 2 Where a party genuinely has difficulty in paying litigation costs, it may, in accordance with the Measures on the Payment of Litigation Costs, apply to the people's court for judicial assistance in the form of deferred payment, reduction, or exemption of litigation costs. Where the circumstances do not meet the conditions for judicial assistance, exemption, reduction, or deferred payment shall not be granted.

Article 3 Litigation fee collection shall strictly implement the principle of "separate management of revenue and expenditure." People's courts at all levels shall, in strict accordance with relevant provisions, promptly turn over litigation fees lawfully collected to the finance department at the same level as required, incorporate them into budgetary management, and shall not open bank accounts for fee collection without authorization, nor intercept, withhold, misappropriate, or privately distribute litigation fees.

Article 4 People's courts at all levels shall, when collecting litigation fees, obtain a fee collection permit from the designated competent pricing department.

Article 5 People's courts at all levels shall strictly implement the relevant provisions on the fee collection publicity system. In the case-filing venue, they shall display the fee collection permit, the scope of litigation costs payable, the items for payment, the standards for payment, as well as the complaint department and telephone number, etc.

Article 6 When collecting litigation fees, people's courts at all levels shall use financial receipts printed by the finance department of the State Council or the finance department of the provincial people's government in accordance with the financial subordination relationship, and shall not privately print or use any other receipts for fee collection.

Article 7 Where a basic people's court's tribunal collects litigation fees on the spot in accordance with relevant provisions, it must issue to the party financial receipts printed by the finance department of the provincial people's government and promptly deposit the collected litigation fees into the designated agency bank.

Article 8 People's courts at all levels shall not collect in advance application fees for enforcement and application fees for bankruptcy in violation of regulations.

Article 9 People's courts at all levels shall, in accordance with actual costs, collect from parties, defenders, and agents, etc., the production costs for duplicating case file materials, audio-visual archives of trial work, and legal documents. The actual costs shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of the provincial pricing and finance departments where the people's court is located.

Article 10 After the settlement of litigation costs, if a people's court at any level is required to refund litigation costs to a party in accordance with regulations, it shall promptly handle the refund procedures; if a case needs to be transferred or handed over after trial, it shall promptly handle the procedures for transferring the litigation costs along with the case, so as not to affect the party's litigation; if a party needs to make supplementary payment of litigation costs, the court shall promptly urge the supplementary payment.

Article 11 People's courts at all levels shall not assign fee collection tasks or targets to internal departments, shall not use the amount of litigation fees collected as a basis for rewards or penalties for departments or individuals, and shall not link the collection of litigation fees with bonuses, welfare, allowances, etc.

Article 12 People's courts at all levels shall conduct an annual self-inspection of the litigation fee collection circumstances of their own court. The higher people's court shall conduct planned inspections of the litigation fee collection circumstances of the courts under its jurisdiction. Problems discovered during inspections shall be promptly corrected.

People's courts at all levels shall, in accordance with relevant provisions, accept and cooperate with the supervision and inspection of litigation fee collection by relevant functional departments.

Article 13 The disciplinary inspection departments of people's courts at all levels are responsible for accepting reports on illegal acts of collecting litigation fees in violation of regulations and investigating and punishing such acts.

Article 14 The disciplinary inspection departments of people's courts at all levels shall conduct serious investigations into acts of collecting litigation fees in violation of regulations. If the facts are verified, they shall impose sanctions on the directly responsible persons in accordance with the relevant disciplinary provisions of the Supreme People's Court. If the illegal collection of litigation fees seriously damages the interests of the parties and causes adverse effects, the responsible leaders and responsible persons shall also be held accountable.

Article 15 These Provisions shall come into effect as of the date of issuance.
